questions.questionText: Which source detail is most useful when checking possible expertise?
options: The author’s relevant qualifications
The background color of the page
The length of the website address
The number and decorative style of images displayed on the page
questions.correctAnswer: The author’s relevant qualifications
questions.explanation: Relevant qualifications help assess whether an author has appropriate knowledge, though expertise does not remove the need to check evidence.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate the credibility, relevance and limitations of sources using authorship, evidence, context and corroboration.

questions.questionText: A company report claims its product reduces emissions. What should a researcher check first for possible bias?
options: Whether the report uses numbered pages and consistent heading styles
The company’s financial interest in the claim
Whether the logo is professionally designed
The time taken to download the file
questions.correctAnswer: The company’s financial interest in the claim
questions.explanation: A direct commercial interest may influence selection or presentation of evidence and should be considered when judging credibility.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate the credibility, relevance and limitations of sources using authorship, evidence, context and corroboration.

questions.questionText: Two independent studies using different methods reach similar conclusions. How does this affect confidence?
options: Different methods make both studies invalid
Agreement proves that neither study has methods or limitations
Corroboration increases confidence in the conclusion
The studies should be treated as one source
questions.correctAnswer: Corroboration increases confidence in the conclusion
questions.explanation: Converging findings from independent methods reduce the likelihood that one method or source alone produced the result.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate the credibility, relevance and limitations of sources using authorship, evidence, context and corroboration.

questions.questionText: An article uses accurate statistics from 15 years ago to describe current internet access. What is its main limitation?
options: All numerical evidence is automatically unreliable
Old evidence can never be used to describe or compare historical change
Internet access cannot be measured
The evidence may no longer represent present conditions
questions.correctAnswer: The evidence may no longer represent present conditions
questions.explanation: Even accurate data can lose relevance when technology and access patterns change rapidly over time.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate the credibility, relevance and limitations of sources using authorship, evidence, context and corroboration.

questions.questionText: What is a perspective?
options: A viewpoint shaped by values and experience
A fixed fact that cannot be questioned or interpreted differently
A random list of unrelated numbers
A rule used only in mathematics
questions.correctAnswer: A viewpoint shaped by values and experience
questions.explanation: A perspective is a way of seeing an issue influenced by experience, values, interests and context.

curriculum.objective: Compare how cultural, social, economic and political contexts shape perspectives on global issues.

questions.questionText: Why might farmers and urban consumers view water pricing differently?
options: Only farmers can understand prices
Their needs, costs and dependence on water differ
Urban consumers never use water
Perspectives are unrelated to interests
questions.correctAnswer: Their needs, costs and dependence on water differ
questions.explanation: Groups experience a policy differently, so economic roles and dependence can shape their judgments.

curriculum.objective: Compare how cultural, social, economic and political contexts shape perspectives on global issues.

questions.questionText: Which response best demonstrates respectful comparison of perspectives?
options: Describe one view as irrational without evidence
Ignore values that differ from your own
Explain each view in context before evaluating it
Assume every group is internally identical
questions.correctAnswer: Explain each view in context before evaluating it
questions.explanation: Fair comparison first represents views accurately and considers the context and reasons behind them.

curriculum.objective: Compare how cultural, social, economic and political contexts shape perspectives on global issues.

questions.questionText: A national survey reports one average opinion for a culturally diverse country. What should a researcher avoid assuming?
options: That surveys can contain quantitative data
That national samples require any planning
That opinions may change over time
That the average represents every subgroup equally
questions.correctAnswer: That the average represents every subgroup equally
questions.explanation: A national mean can hide regional, cultural or demographic differences and should not be assigned to every subgroup.

curriculum.objective: Compare how cultural, social, economic and political contexts shape perspectives on global issues.

questions.questionText: Which method is best for exploring detailed personal experiences?
options: Semi-structured interview
Closed numerical tally only
Automated file compression
Random password generation
questions.correctAnswer: Semi-structured interview
questions.explanation: Semi-structured interviews allow consistent topics while giving participants space to explain experiences in depth.

curriculum.objective: Select and apply ethical quantitative and qualitative research methods using valid sampling, questions and data handling.

questions.questionText: Which survey question is leading?
options: How often do you recycle each week?
How much do you support the excellent recycling plan?
Which recycling service do you use?
What is your age group?
questions.correctAnswer: How much do you support the excellent recycling plan?
questions.explanation: Calling the plan excellent encourages approval and biases responses rather than asking neutrally.

curriculum.objective: Select and apply ethical quantitative and qualitative research methods using valid sampling, questions and data handling.

questions.questionText: Why is informed consent important in human research?
options: It guarantees every participant agrees with results
It removes the need to protect personal data
Participants understand the study and choose freely
It allows researchers to hide all risks
questions.correctAnswer: Participants understand the study and choose freely
questions.explanation: Informed consent requires adequate information, voluntary participation and awareness of relevant risks and rights.

curriculum.objective: Select and apply ethical quantitative and qualitative research methods using valid sampling, questions and data handling.

questions.questionText: A student surveys only close friends about school rules. Which problem most threatens generalization?
options: Friends can never answer any survey
The sample contains qualitative opinions
School rules cannot be researched
Convenience sampling creates selection bias
questions.correctAnswer: Convenience sampling creates selection bias
questions.explanation: Close friends may share similar experiences and views, so they are unlikely to represent the wider student population.

curriculum.objective: Select and apply ethical quantitative and qualitative research methods using valid sampling, questions and data handling.

questions.questionText: What is evidence in an argument?
options: Information used to support a claim
The title of every document
A conclusion with no reasons
A personal attack on an opponent
questions.correctAnswer: Information used to support a claim
questions.explanation: Evidence consists of information or observations offered as support for a claim or conclusion.

curriculum.objective: Construct and assess arguments by distinguishing claims, evidence, assumptions, counterarguments and reasoning errors.

questions.questionText: Which statement is an assumption in the argument “The library should open later because students need quiet study space”?
options: The library currently has a door
Later opening will provide usable quiet study time
Some students own pens
Books are arranged on shelves
questions.correctAnswer: Later opening will provide usable quiet study time
questions.explanation: The reasoning depends on the unstated link that later hours would meet students’ need for quiet study space.

curriculum.objective: Construct and assess arguments by distinguishing claims, evidence, assumptions, counterarguments and reasoning errors.

questions.questionText: A speaker dismisses a climate proposal because its author is young. Which reasoning error is this?
options: Using a representative random sample
Drawing a conclusion from direct measurements
Attacking the person instead of the argument
Acknowledging a strong counterargument
questions.correctAnswer: Attacking the person instead of the argument
questions.explanation: The author’s age does not address the proposal’s evidence or reasoning, so the response is an ad hominem attack.

curriculum.objective: Construct and assess arguments by distinguishing claims, evidence, assumptions, counterarguments and reasoning errors.

questions.questionText: Which revision most strengthens an argument with a serious counterclaim?
options: Pretend the counterclaim does not exist
Repeat the original claim more loudly
Replace evidence with an unrelated anecdote
Address the counterclaim using relevant evidence
questions.correctAnswer: Address the counterclaim using relevant evidence
questions.explanation: Engaging directly with a credible objection shows why the conclusion remains justified or needs qualification.

curriculum.objective: Construct and assess arguments by distinguishing claims, evidence, assumptions, counterarguments and reasoning errors.

questions.questionText: What is the clearest benefit of assigning roles in a team project?
options: Responsibilities become visible and coordinated
Every member completes identical work
The project no longer needs a goal
Disagreement becomes impossible
questions.correctAnswer: Responsibilities become visible and coordinated
questions.explanation: Clear roles help distribute work, reduce duplication and make accountability easier to manage.

curriculum.objective: Collaborate to plan, implement and evaluate responsible action using roles, stakeholders, evidence and reflection.

questions.questionText: A team wants to reduce cafeteria waste. What should it do before choosing an intervention?
options: Print posters before defining the problem
Collect baseline evidence about types and amounts of waste
Assume one solution works in every school
Measure results only before the project
questions.correctAnswer: Collect baseline evidence about types and amounts of waste
questions.explanation: Baseline data identifies the scale and causes of the problem and later provides a comparison for evaluating change.

curriculum.objective: Collaborate to plan, implement and evaluate responsible action using roles, stakeholders, evidence and reflection.

questions.questionText: Which indicator best measures whether a reusable-cup campaign changed behavior?
options: Number of colors in the campaign logo
Length of the final presentation
Change in disposable cups used per customer
Total followers of an unrelated account
questions.correctAnswer: Change in disposable cups used per customer
questions.explanation: This outcome indicator directly measures the target behavior while accounting for changes in customer numbers.

curriculum.objective: Collaborate to plan, implement and evaluate responsible action using roles, stakeholders, evidence and reflection.

questions.questionText: A project met its target but excluded a stakeholder group affected by the action. What is the strongest evaluation?
options: The target proves the process was fully ethical
Stakeholder participation never affects quality
The project cannot have produced any useful result
The outcome succeeded, but the process lacked inclusion
questions.correctAnswer: The outcome succeeded, but the process lacked inclusion
questions.explanation: Evaluation should distinguish outcome achievement from weaknesses in participation, fairness and legitimacy.

curriculum.objective: Collaborate to plan, implement and evaluate responsible action using roles, stakeholders, evidence and reflection.
